bug_semantics: The authenticated /deploy/fileDiff endpoint accepted attacker-controlled filePath without a server-side relative-path or containment check. It joined that value to the local project directory for ioutil.ReadFile and to the managed server's project.Path for SFTP Open, so ../ traversal escaped both intended roots and returned local and remote file contents as srcText and distText.
flaw_origin: Commit 16f6e848b8cb08a48f64cdc077a286ed6d75e722 introduced the FileDiff feature and, in the same new function, directly passed reqData.FilePath into both local path.Join plus ioutil.ReadFile and remote path.Join plus sftpClient.Open. The immediate parent contains no FileDiff route/function or srcText/distText mechanism, making this feature commit the smallest surviving public first-write of the vulnerable mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: raw BIC commit object shows author and committer zhenorzz <zhenorzz@gmail.com>, subject 'A file compare', an empty body, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: Vendor advisory https://github.com/zhenorzz/goploy/security/advisories/GHSA-4g5x-hcwm-82jw is published, High severity, identifies CVE-2026-53553, affects <=1.17.5, and describes authenticated ../ traversal through /deploy/fileDiff that returns local srcText and remote distText; its live page and GitHub reviewed advisory are not withdrawn or rejected.

git show 16f6e848b8cb08a48f64cdc077a286ed6d75e722 -- controller/DeployController.go shows the newly added FileDiff function at controller/DeployController.go:240-291, including ioutil.ReadFile(path.Join(core.GetProjectPath(reqData.ProjectID), reqData.FilePath)) and sftpClient.Open(path.Join(project.Path, reqData.FilePath)) with no server-side path validation.

git log -L :FileDiff:controller/DeployController.go and git log -S 'func (Deploy) FileDiff' --follow identify 16f6e848b8cb08a48f64cdc077a286ed6d75e722 (2021-12-09, 'A file compare') as the first public commit of FileDiff; later 05c15c06abff8b43cc8d4a4f4089fed0e2c1a298 and 29ec736e47ddb5033ea294e3ee2f237f0e70da76 are file-structure moves/refactors, not introducers.

Direct parent-tree check: git grep -n 'FileDiff\|fileDiff\|srcText\|distText' 16b40bbc400f7f34f557ed2064365c834061d47f -- '*.go' '*.ts' '*.vue' returns zero matches, while the BIC tree contains the new route, backend function, both read sinks, response fields, API client, and UI.

git cat-file commit 16f6e848b8cb08a48f64cdc077a286ed6d75e722 shows one parent, author/committer zhenorzz <zhenorzz@gmail.com>, subject 'A file compare', and no body or trailers; no commit-object AI marker exists. The commit is the smallest surviving public feature object and exposes no reconstructable finer member history.

git show d51aa15ebc0a474d9d71d6c453a0fe798dd5e007 adds pkg.ValidateRelativePath(reqData.FilePath) immediately before FileDiff resolves either project path; internal/pkg/util.go rejects null bytes, Unix/Windows absolute paths, '..', and cleaned '../' prefixes, directly blocking the advisory traversal mechanism. Its parent 5438ef05777e1d3b1e1ed2fa0892a39b4cb3161a has no ValidateRelativePath symbol.

Tag topology: 16f6e848b8cb08a48f64cdc077a286ed6d75e722 is an ancestor of vulnerable tag v1.17.5 (3220b64795f8d90674b9052d2310ede778028c77); d51aa15ebc0a474d9d71d6c453a0fe798dd5e007 is not an ancestor of v1.17.5 but is the parent of and an ancestor of v1.18.0 (4c682981730fb74d599a5cd84a094c5ba6fd4b89). The v1.18.0 vendor release notes explicitly list prevention of GHSA-4g5x-hcwm-82jw path traversal.

CVE.org record URL https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53553 was checked on 2026-08-29; the public endpoint exposed only its JavaScript shell and the official cvelistV5 record path was not yet present. This does not contradict the vendor-published, GitHub-reviewed, non-withdrawn advisory or the independently verified vulnerable and fixed trees.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and its lifecycle is closed in first-party history. The BIC introduced an authenticated comparison feature but trusted filePath at both local and remote filesystem sinks, allowing traversal out of each project root and disclosure in the response. Line and string history trace that mechanism through later refactors back to single-parent commit 16f6e848b8cb08a48f64cdc077a286ed6d75e722; its immediate parent lacks the complete feature and vulnerable lines. Commit d51aa15ebc0a474d9d71d6c453a0fe798dd5e007 directly fixes the same data flow by validating filePath before both sinks, and release topology matches <=1.17.5 affected with the fix included in v1.18.0 despite the advisory's patched-version metadata still saying None. The BIC commit object has only the human zhenorzz identity and no AI authorship/co-authorship marker, so the correct BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI; the later fix and later AI-signaled repository activity are irrelevant to attribution.
